discovery: Prediction and discovery of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators
subfield: Condensed matter physics (topological phases of matter)
motivation: In 2005 Kane and Mele showed, with a strikingly simple model of graphene with spin-orbit coupling, that time-reversal-invariant insulators carry a hidden Z2 topological invariant, implying a quantum spin Hall state with protected helical edge channels. This turned Berry-curvature band topology from a quantum Hall curiosity requiring strong magnetic fields into a general property of ordinary materials. In 2007 Molenkamp's group observed quantized edge conduction in HgTe quantum wells, confirming the prediction experimentally. The concept was rapidly generalised to three-dimensional topological insulators, now found in many compounds, and underlies the quantum anomalous Hall effect, topological superconductivity proposals, and topological classification of band structures across physics. It is a model case of theory and experiment advancing together: a transparent prediction, a decisive measurement, and a field that has reshaped how condensed-matter physicists think about electronic states of matter.
